threats.title: Cross-customer PII disclosure through suggested-reply model memorization
threats.description: Transcripts are exported from the helpdesk into the training store in full, including customer names, email addresses, and complete message bodies, and no redaction or filtering step exists between the helpdesk and the training store. The weekly tuning job fine-tunes the vendor's base model directly on the training store's current contents, and the reply service serves the resulting artifact to generate one suggested reply per open ticket, which the agent may use with or without edits. Because the fine-tuning corpus is raw, unredacted ticket text containing direct identifiers, the tuned model can memorize and later reproduce fragments of individual training examples in its output. A support agent working one customer's ticket could be shown, and act on, a suggested reply that reproduces a name, email address, or message fragment drawn from a different customer's earlier, unrelated ticket.
preconditions: Transcripts are exported and stored without redaction or filtering of direct identifiers such as names, email addresses, and message bodies.
The tuning job fine-tunes directly on this unredacted corpus with no documented data-minimization step before training.
The fine-tuned reply model is capable of reproducing memorized fragments of individual training examples in generated text, a known behavior of models fine-tuned on raw text corpora.
attack_path: Customer writes ticket messages containing personal data during normal support interaction.
Nightly exporter writes the closed ticket's full, unredacted transcript into the training store.
Weekly tuning job fine-tunes the vendor base model on the training store's contents, including this record.
The fine-tuned model memorizes a distinctive fragment of the record.
Reply service generates a suggested reply for an unrelated open ticket that reproduces the memorized fragment.
Agent views the suggestion and uses it, with or without edits, in a reply to a different customer.
threats.impact: Disclosure of one customer's personal data (name, email address, or verbatim message text) to a support agent, and potentially onward to a different customer, via a suggested reply generated by a model trained on the first customer's unredacted transcript — a confidentiality impact on the Exported Ticket Transcripts asset realized through the Tuned Model Artifact.

threats.title: Training-data poisoning via compromise of the exporter's sole write identity
threats.description: Write access to the training store is restricted to a single principal, the transcript exporter's job identity, enforced through the platform's access policy; no other write-side control, such as content validation or provenance checking, is documented. The weekly tuning job fine-tunes on the training store's current contents as a whole. If the exporter's job identity or its execution context were obtained or abused by another party, that party could write fabricated or altered transcript records into the training store indistinguishable from genuine exports, and those records would be trained into the next artifact and served to every agent once promoted as most recent.
preconditions: The training store accepts writes from a single principal with no documented secondary control on the content written.
The exporter's job identity or its execution context can be obtained or abused by a party other than the intended nightly export process, a condition the documentation does not address either way.
No content-integrity check between export and training is documented.
attack_path: An external party obtains or abuses the exporter's job identity, the sole principal with write access to the training store.
The party writes fabricated or altered transcript records into the training store using that identity.
The weekly tuning job fine-tunes on the store's current contents without distinguishing genuine from injected records.
The resulting artifact, carrying the injected influence, is written to the artifact bucket.
The reply service begins serving the new artifact as the most recent one.
threats.impact: Introduction of attacker-controlled content into the training corpus and, subsequently, into the tuned model artifact served to all agents — an integrity impact on the Exporter Job Write Identity, the Exported Ticket Transcripts, and the Tuned Model Artifact.

threats.title: Undocumented read-access scope on the training store
threats.description: The documentation establishes that write access to the training store is restricted to the exporter's job identity alone, but says nothing about which principals may read the bucket's full, unredacted contents, and no overall authorization posture for the system is established in the material. The store holds complete transcripts, including customer names, email addresses, and message bodies, organized simply by export date. Any principal with read access to the bucket beyond the tuning job — a platform operator, a broader grant under the same access policy, or another job — could retrieve the raw personal data directly, without the reply-generation pipeline mediating anything.
preconditions: Read access to the training store is not documented; only write access is described, and only as restricted to the exporter's job identity.
No system-wide authorization model is established in the documentation.
The bucket holds full, unredacted personal data with no documented reader-side restriction beyond the general platform access policy named for the component.
attack_path: A principal other than the tuning job, holding platform access not documented as excluded from the training store, is granted or retains read access to the bucket.
That principal reads the bucket's contents directly, bypassing the training and serving pipeline.
The principal obtains full-fidelity transcripts, including direct customer identifiers.
threats.impact: Direct exposure of full-fidelity customer personal data — names, email addresses, message content — to a broader set of principals than the reply-generation pipeline requires, independent of the training or serving process.

threats.title: Interception or modification of the nightly transcript export in transit
threats.description: The nightly export from the helpdesk to the transcript exporter carries full ticket transcripts, including customer names, email addresses, and message bodies, and crosses the documented helpdesk/pipeline trust boundary. The data flow's authentication and its encryption in transit are both recorded as unknown, and the only control documented at this boundary is the platform's access policy, which is not established as governing this transport. If the flow lacks authentication of the source or encryption in transit, a party positioned on the path between the helpdesk and the exporter, or one able to impersonate either endpoint, could read or alter the transcripts as they move, before any pipeline-side control applies.
preconditions: Authentication for the helpdesk-to-exporter export is recorded as unknown.
Encryption in transit for the same flow is recorded as unknown.
The only documented control at the boundary this flow crosses is the platform access policy, whose coverage of this specific transport is not stated.
attack_path: The helpdesk initiates the nightly export of closed-ticket transcripts toward the exporter.
The transcripts cross the helpdesk/pipeline trust boundary over a channel whose authentication and encryption are not established in the documentation.
A party positioned on that path, or able to impersonate an endpoint, reads or modifies the transcripts before they reach the exporter.
threats.impact: Disclosure or undetected modification of full ticket transcripts, including direct customer identifiers, in transit between the helpdesk and the pipeline — a confidentiality and integrity impact on the Exported Ticket Transcripts asset at its point of entry.

threats.title: Compromise of the vendor-supplied base model propagates through every served artifact
threats.description: The tuning job fine-tunes the vendor's base reply model, supplied across the vendor boundary. Unlike the helpdesk boundary, which documents the platform access policy as a control, the vendor boundary lists no controls at all, and the flow carrying the base model weights records both authentication and encryption in transit as unknown. The tuning job fine-tunes directly on top of this externally supplied model and writes the result to the artifact bucket, from which the reply service automatically serves whichever artifact is most recent. A compromised, backdoored, or substituted base model — whether from a vendor-side compromise or an unverified supply channel — would be inherited by every weekly artifact and reach every agent's console with no documented integrity check at the point of receipt.
preconditions: The vendor boundary documents no controls, in contrast to the helpdesk boundary which documents the platform access policy.
Authentication and encryption in transit for the base-model supply flow are both recorded as unknown.
No integrity or provenance verification of the received base model is documented before it is used as the fine-tuning starting point.
attack_path: The model vendor supplies a base model across the vendor boundary over a channel with unestablished authentication and encryption, or a party substitutes one along that path.
The tuning job receives the base model and uses it as the starting point for fine-tuning, without a documented integrity check.
The tuning job writes the resulting artifact, inheriting any compromise in the base model, to the artifact bucket.
The reply service serves the artifact, and the compromised behavior reaches every agent's console.
threats.impact: A compromised or substituted base model shapes every weekly tuned artifact and every suggested reply generated system-wide — an integrity impact on the Tuned Model Artifact with no documented check at the point the base model enters the pipeline.

threats.title: Automatic promotion of the most recent artifact without a documented validation gate
threats.description: The reply service serves whichever artifact in the artifact bucket is most recent, and the documentation does not state whether any validation, testing, or approval occurs between the tuning job writing an artifact and the reply service beginning to serve it. If no such gate exists, any defective, degraded, or compromised artifact — whether from a bad tuning run, poisoned training data, or a compromised base model — is promoted to production the moment it is written, with no described mechanism to catch or roll back a bad promotion before agents see its output.
preconditions: Whether the reply service validates an artifact before serving it is not established in the documentation.
Artifacts are promoted by recency alone, named by date, with no documented approval step.
attack_path: The tuning job completes a run and writes a new artifact to the artifact bucket.
The reply service identifies this artifact as the most recent and begins serving it.
No described validation, testing, or approval step intervenes between these two events.
Any defect or compromise present in the artifact is now live for every open ticket.
threats.impact: A defective or compromised weekly artifact reaches every agent's console and shapes every suggested reply for a full cycle before the next tuning run, with no documented mechanism to detect or roll back the promotion — an integrity and availability impact on the Tuned Model Artifact.

threats.title: Unredacted transcript data may leave the environment if fine-tuning executes on vendor infrastructure
threats.description: The documentation states that the tuning job fine-tunes the vendor's base reply model but does not state whether that fine-tuning executes within the pipeline's own environment or by calling out to the vendor's infrastructure; this question was put to the reviewer directly and returned no substantive answer, so the execution location remains undetermined by the record. If fine-tuning is performed on vendor-hosted infrastructure rather than locally, the unredacted transcripts held in the training store — including customer names, email addresses, and full message bodies — would need to be transmitted to the vendor to serve as training input, a cross-boundary flow of personal data that is not represented among the documented data flows and whose protections, if any, are therefore entirely unestablished.
preconditions: Whether fine-tuning executes within the pipeline's own environment or on vendor infrastructure is not established in the documentation.
A direct question to the reviewer on this point returned no substantive answer, leaving the condition open.
If execution is vendor-hosted, transcript data would need to leave the environment to reach the vendor, a flow not represented among the documented data flows.
attack_path: The tuning job invokes fine-tuning against the vendor's base model at a location the documentation does not establish as internal or vendor-hosted.
If execution is vendor-hosted, the training store's unredacted transcripts are transmitted to the vendor to serve as fine-tuning input.
This transmission, if it occurs, is governed by no control stated in the documented architecture.
threats.impact: If realized, disclosure of the full unredacted transcript corpus, including direct customer identifiers, to a third party beyond the boundary the documentation otherwise describes as containing this data — a confidentiality impact on the Exported Ticket Transcripts asset.

threats.title: Customer-authored ticket content becomes unfiltered fine-tuning input
threats.description: Any customer can write ticket messages, and closed-ticket transcripts are exported into the training store in full, with no redaction or filtering step between the helpdesk and the training store, before the weekly tuning job fine-tunes the base model on the training store's current contents. Because the pipeline treats all closed-ticket text as ordinary training signal, a customer could word ticket messages deliberately to influence the fine-tuned model's future behavior — for example, phrasing intended to bias the tone or content of suggested replies the model later produces for other agents and other tickets — using only the ordinary support channel already open to them, without needing any elevated access or credential.
preconditions: Any customer can write arbitrary ticket message content, which becomes part of a closed ticket and is exported as training data.
No redaction or filtering step exists between the helpdesk and the training store.
The tuning job trains on the store's contents as a whole, with no documented per-example vetting.
attack_path: A customer writes ticket message content phrased to influence future model behavior, using the ordinary support channel.
The ticket is closed and its full transcript is exported into the training store unredacted and unfiltered.
The weekly tuning job fine-tunes on the store's contents, incorporating the crafted text as ordinary training signal.
The fine-tuned model's future suggested replies, for other tickets and other customers, reflect the influence of the crafted content.
threats.impact: Skewing of the suggested-reply model's output for unrelated tickets and other customers, introduced through an input channel that requires no elevated access — an integrity impact on the Tuned Model Artifact traceable to the unfiltered Exported Ticket Transcripts.
